fields.meta_title: Customer Feedback Survey That Sorts Comments | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a customer feedback survey that sorts comments by theme, saves each answer with its customer and routes complaints to an owner.
fields.h1: Build a Customer Feedback Survey and Act on Every Comment
fields.hero_description: Describe who you want to hear from and when. Emergent builds the questions, the trigger that sends them and the rules that route each comment, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Feedback Survey Has to Do
fields.features_subheading: A customer feedback survey asks customers rated and open questions about a recent experience. The comments teach the most.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from your goal

Describe what you need to learn and from whom. Emergent writes a rating and an open question, plus a reason list if you want one. Change any question by describing the edit.
fields.feature_2:
Sends tied to real events

Start the survey when a subscription is canceled or a job closes in your dispatch tool. Any tool with an API can trigger a send, and each send is logged against the customer.
fields.feature_3:
Comments sorted by type and theme

Tag every open answer by type, such as a bug or a complaint, then group it by theme with a count. A product lead reads 15 themes instead of scrolling through 400 comments.
fields.feature_4:
Context saved with each answer

Store the customer ID and plan with every response, plus the order, store or technician involved. Filter by any of them to see where one complaint keeps coming from.
fields.feature_5:
Complaints sent to one owner

Route a low rating, or a comment that mentions a refund, to the person who can fix it. The Slack message or email carries the comment and the full customer record with it.
fields.feature_6:
Code and answers you can take with you

Answers live in a database you own, with no response cap. Export the survey and its sorting rules to your GitHub repository, along with every answer collected so far.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Feedback Survey With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A feedback survey is worth what happens to its comments. Emergent builds it as an app you control, with no cap on answers.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places to Ask for Feedback
fields.tab_content_1:
Find out why subscribers cancel

Once Stripe reports a canceled subscription, the subscriber gets a three-question email: the main reason, what would bring them back and anything else. Each answer is saved with the plan and months subscribed. Over 30 days, 112 of 160 canceling subscribers answered, and price led with 41.
fields.tab_content_2:
In-app comments, sorted before anyone reads them

A feedback button sits on every screen of your web app. Each comment is saved with the page and the account's plan, then tagged as a bug, idea, question or praise. When one bug is reported 9 times in a week, the product team's Slack channel gets the count and the comments.
fields.tab_content_3:
A text after every repair visit

Two hours after the technician closes the job, the customer gets a text through Twilio. It asks for a star rating, whether the tech arrived in the booked window and what went wrong, if anything. A rating of 2 or lower becomes a callback task for the dispatcher, with the job number and the comment.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which store slipped this week, and why

Shoppers at all 12 stores scan a QR code printed on the receipt and answer four questions on their phone. Answers roll up by store each week. When a store's score falls more than 0.5 points, its district manager gets an email with the drop and the most common complaint.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Customer Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is deciding what the answers will change and who reads them. Write both down first; Emergent builds the survey and its routing around them.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one decision the answers should settle, such as which cancellation reason to fix first or which store needs a visit. A survey without one collects opinions nobody owns. Put that decision at the top of your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send it at the cancellation or the closed job, while the details are fresh. Feedback requested weeks later is about memory more than the visit. One short survey per moment works better than an annual questionnaire covering everything.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Use one rating and one open question. Add a reason list only once the same answers start repeating. Ask about one thing per question: rating the technician and the price together gives a number nobody can read. Put the open question after the rating, where it asks why.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Run the survey open-ended with a small group first. Recurring answers become the choices in your reason list. For a coffee subscription that could be price or too much coffee. The open box stays for everything the list misses.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the customer ID and the order or job number along with the survey link. A comment that says the tech came late again only helps when it arrives with the technician and the booked window attached.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give every comment type an owner
fields.howto_step_6_des: Bugs go to the product channel, cancellation reasons to the retention lead and low visit ratings to the dispatcher. Set a threshold for each owner. Nine reports of one bug deserve a message; one vague complaint can wait for the weekly read.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the comments before the scores
fields.howto_step_7_des: A rating says something went wrong, and the comment says what. Read the largest themes each week, then tell customers what changed because they answered. Edit the questions by prompting when one answer keeps arriving.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists, glossary definitions and survey-tool landing pages (easy-feedback, QuickTapSurvey, LimeSurvey). None shows what happens to the open-text answers. This page answers the PAA questions (how to write one, the three C's, how to analyze feedback, the types of feedback) and then shows four feedback surveys whose comments get read and routed: a cancellation survey fed by Stripe, an in-app feedback button sorted by type, a text after a technician's visit, and a QR survey across 12 retail stores. The live customer-satisfaction sibling owns CSAT, NPS and CES scoring at onboarding, post-purchase, B2B quarterly and ticket close; this page owns open-ended feedback and why customers leave, complain or ask.
